IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Window_Body:
This window explains the vehicle upgrades of Standardized Vehicle Upgrades 3 (SVU3). It only shows information: you still install and remove upgrades in the Modifications window (vehicle radial menu > Modifications).
It opens by itself beside the Modifications window and closes with it. Turn that off in Options > Mods > HARMONIE - Car for Crash. There you can also set a key that opens it for the car you sit in or stand next to.
Tabs: This car - its tier, stats, installed upgrades and your skills. Upgrades - everything this car can take. Vehicle tiers - every car by tier. Guide - this guide.
IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Tiers_Body:
Every car SVU3 can upgrade gets a tier from 1 (small) to 3 (large). Each car is compared with all the others in four stats from its vehicle script: weight, front + rear strength, seats and trunk size. Its places in these stats are averaged and the list is cut into three equal parts. Cars with the same stats are always in the same tier.
If the game cannot read a stat (for example the trunk size), that stat is left out. A car with no readable stats is tier 3. An admin can also put cars in a tier by hand (see Admin settings).
The bars in This car show where the car sits among all cars: full = the highest of all.
The tier of every car is also written to console.txt when the game starts.
IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Skills_Body:
Each upgrade needs some skill levels to install. The highest one is its main skill (mostly Metalworking). The others are its second skills (mostly Mechanics, sometimes Electrical).
Each tier has a ceiling for the main skill and for the second skills. The defaults are tier 1 = 4 + 2, tier 2 = 6 + 4 and tier 3 = 8 + 6. SVU3's hardest upgrade (the plow, 8 + 6) needs exactly the ceiling. Easier upgrades need less, in the same proportion, rounded, and never below 1.
Examples: the plow is 4+2 / 6+4 / 8+6, the large bullbar (SVU3: 6+4) is 3+1 / 5+3 / 6+4, reinforced armour (SVU3: 8) is 4 / 6 / 8.
In the Upgrades tab each skill shows what it needs and, in brackets, your level: green = enough, red = not yet. Removing an upgrade needs SVU3's own levels.
IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Time_Body:
Each upgrade has a time value from SVU3: 15 for light parts and most add-ons, 30 for heavy armour and 45 for reinforced armour. These come from SVU3's own sandbox options (page SVUC) and can be changed there.
Your Mechanics level makes it faster: every level takes 1/15 off. At Mechanics 0 it takes the full time, at 5 two thirds (x0.67), at 10 one third (x0.33). The skill levels an upgrade needs do not change its time.
Removing an upgrade takes the same time as installing it.
IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Materials_Body:
Every upgrade uses up materials (metal pipes, metal bars, screws, sheet metal, propane torch uses...) and needs tools (wrench and screwdriver; a welder mask when it is welded). The Upgrades tab lists them on each row; point at the list for the full names.
This window does not check whether you carry them. The Modifications window checks that, and it greys out an upgrade until everything is at hand.
Some upgrades need another one first (for example a scoop hood needs its hood armour). Those show Install ... first.
IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Wear_Body:
Armour and bullbars from SVU3 lose condition each time they take a hit for the part they protect. The sandbox option Protection part damage multiplier (page HARMONIE - Car for Crash) sets how fast: 1.0 = SVU3's own wear, higher = they wear out faster.
The condition of every installed upgrade is shown in This car. Some parts fall off when they break.
IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Admin_Body:
Sandbox options, page HARMONIE: SVU3 Part Wear:
- Install skills by vehicle tier: on = the tiers above; off = every car needs SVU3's own levels.
- Tier 1 / 2 / 3 main skill and other skills: the ceilings (default 4+2, 6+4, 8+6).
- Vehicle tiers set by hand: name=tier separated by ; for example Van*=2; StepVan=3. A * at the end means every car whose name starts so (Van* = Van, VanAmbulance, Van_Glass...). An exact name wins over a * one. none = nothing set by hand. The script names are in console.txt and under the car's name in This car.
- Protection part damage multiplier: how fast armour wears (see Part wear).
IGUI_HSVU_Guide_Buttons_Body:
Top right: A- and A+ change the text size, the pin keeps the window open, X closes it.
Unpinned, the window folds up to its title bar a moment after the mouse leaves it, and opens again when the mouse comes back.
Drag the title bar to move the window. Drag the bottom-right corner to resize it; right-click that corner for the default size. The mouse wheel scrolls long lists.
The size, text size and pin are remembered on this computer.
